<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:storyscope" data-paper-title="StoryScope: Investigating idiosyncrasies in AI fiction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-00b20bade33adf0d">Where do StoryScope and DetectorScope obtain interpretability, and are their features interchangeable?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Astoryscope">StoryScope: Investigating idiosyncrasies in AI fiction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-13 · University of Maryland, College Park</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>StoryScope uses externally assigned semantic narrative questions with classifier/SHAP analysis. DetectorScope uses internal SAE features and an additive sparse head. Their explanation units, costs and errors differ; random SAE columns cannot replace uncomputed narrative assignments.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: deciding whether an ending states its theme requires semantic reading. The contribution of a numbered SAE column is a separate observation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.03136v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2604.03136-storyscope/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-00b20bade33adf0d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:storyscope" data-paper-title="StoryScope: Investigating idiosyncrasies in AI fiction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-bbd0eae682f39c8b">Why bootstrap all six source stories sharing a prompt together?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Astoryscope">StoryScope: Investigating idiosyncrasies in AI fiction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-13 · University of Maryland, College Park</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They share a writing condition rather than forming six independent arbitrary rows. Split by prompt first, then resample prompt blocks and expand all sources. Story-level sampling or cross-split prompt overlap can inflate apparent independent evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: selecting prompt A twice includes its human story and all five AI stories twice, not only whichever versions favor a stable feature.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 数据协议与代码映射. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.03136v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2604.03136-storyscope/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bbd0eae682f39c8b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>

<details class="ar-learning-guide" markdown="1"><summary>Topic guide and reading order</summary>

## Start with this question

How can we tell whether a high score reflects the intended capability rather than language, ordering, readout, or statistical bias?

## Takeaway

XLGoBench holds the underlying task constant with comparable multilingual algorithmic problems and objective answers, then varies language and complexity. ProEval fits a probabilistic surrogate from past item scores and uses uncertainty to select informative inputs, saving expensive ratings. Activation probes, reranking calibration, and watermarks audit other observation channels. Define the target capability and observable first.

## Example

Translate a shortest-path problem while keeping the graph and correct path fixed. If quality drops, check that the translation preserved constraints. A 100-item budget can use active selection, but then the selected set is not representative. Use the prescribed estimator and uncertainty, not the raw average on difficult cases.

## Common pitfall

Detection scores, operator contract pass rates, and model capability are different. Surrogates may use history but not unseen target scores or gold. One cross-language difference is not a full language-capability claim. Local ProEval and XLGoBench scorer diagnostics do not reproduce the full papers.

## Reading order

Start with XLGoBench on controlled task, language, and difficulty. Then read ProEval on GP surrogates, active selection, and population estimation. Follow with probing, calibration, safety detection, or online experiments.

1. [XLGoBench: Detecting cross-lingual skill gaps with algorithmic tasks](../../../../foundation-models/2605.30788-xlgobench/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.30788v1)
2. [ProEval: Proactive Failure Discovery and Efficient Performance Estimation for Generative AI Evaluation](../../../../foundation-models/2604.23099-proeval/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.23099)

## Check your understanding

If actively selected likely failures have low mean accuracy, can we directly estimate overall online accuracy?

??? note "Show suggested answer"

    No. Selection by failure likelihood introduces bias. Define the target distribution and use a matching estimator or representative sample. Report failure discovery and overall estimation separately.
